title: Heal•Thy.
subtitle: An app centralizing all of your healthy lifestyle information without complicating the task.

glance.Problem: Health apps overflow with dense content. People want ease of use and more detail without stress.
glance.Contribution: Personal project: interviews, competitive analysis, card sorting, flows, wireframes and prototype.
glance.Outcome: A simple app concept with four mapped flows, annotated wireframes and a prototype.

sections.label: Problem statement
sections.heading: Centralize healthy lifestyle information without complicating it.
paras: Heal•Thy is meant to simplify an oversaturated information landscape by bringing healthy lifestyle information into one place.

sections.label: Research
sections.heading: User interviews and competitive analysis.
paras: Interviewees focused mainly on healthy eating. The most experienced participant was the only one who ate when she wanted and didn't let outside factors change that. Only one person mentioned an app.
I concluded that people are less interested in tracking food and more influenced by eating what suits their body.

sections.label: Competitive analysis
sections.heading: Competitors overflow with content and features.
paras: Combined with the interview findings, this told me people want ease of use and more detail without stress.

sections.label: Problem statement pivot
sections.heading: Serve beginners and experienced people alike.
paras: The problem is still how people gain knowledge about having a healthy relationship with food. Instead of focusing only on people who lack knowledge, the app also serves people with health experience who want to keep growing.

sections.label: Card sorting
sections.heading: How people categorize their diets and food choices.
paras: I ran a card sorting exercise to see how interviewees categorize their diets and food choices.

sections.label: Affinity mapping and persona
sections.heading: From interview notes to a persona.
paras: I created an affinity map and a persona from the research.

sections.label: MoSCoW method
sections.heading: Prioritizing features.
paras: I prioritized features using the MoSCoW method.

sections.label: User flows
sections.heading: Four flows: onboarding, article, user settings and library.
